title: TypeScript SDK progressive hydration: resumable WebStream <-> AsyncIterator bridge with retry checkpoints
creator: Sana Patel
description: Add a progressive hydration API in the TypeScript SDK that converts WHATWG ReadableStreams (Web Streams) into AsyncIterables and vice versa while providing lightweight checkpoints for retry-safe resumes and explicit backpressure hints. The feature targets production use-cases where downstream consumers may need to retry from a known checkpoint without reprocessing large prefixes, and where client code wants ergonomic cancellation + cooperative backpressure across runtime environments (Node, Deno, browser).
background: Existing SDK adapters cover most async iterable and Web Stream interop cases, but we still see common customer friction: 1) retries for long streaming responses require restarting from scratch; 2) complex glue in apps to propagate cancellation and partial checkpoints; 3) varying backpressure behavior across runtimes causing token bursts. This ticket designs a bridge that emits small, verifiable checkpoints during streaming and exposes a single ergonomic conversion primitive for consumers (progressive hydration).
proposal: Implement `progressiveHydrate(stream, opts)` and `checkpointedAsyncIterator(source, opts)` primitives: - `progressiveHydrate` accepts a ReadableStream and yields AsyncIterable items while emitting ephemeral checkpoint tokens (opaque string) at configurable intervals (time/byte/token/semantic delimiter). Checkpoints are stable for the server-side request and can be passed to a retry/fallback API to request the remaining suffix. - `checkpointedAsyncIterator` wraps an AsyncIterable and exposes an attachable `CheckpointController` that the SDK can serialize into requests when resuming. Both primitives will carry a small metadata header on each chunk (`{ checkpoint?: string, seq: number }`) but keep the payload ergonomically the original user object (string/chunk/JSON). We will provide default checkpoint frequency tuned for short-latency apps (approx every 256-1024 tokens or 200ms), and allow customers to opt into semantic-checkpoint mode (flush on newline or JSON end).
implementation_notes: API shape: keep public surface minimal: progressiveHydrate(stream, opts) returns AsyncIterable<{ data: string | Uint8Array | object, checkpoint?: string, seq: number }>

Under the hood: use a small sliding buffer + token/byte counters. Emit checkpoint token as base64url HMAC(prefixDigest || seq) to ensure opaqueness and tamper resistance. Backend will later map that token to a stream cursor; SDK does not need to interpret contents.

Cancellation: wire AbortSignal propagation into both directions. When consumer calls return() on the iterator, close underlying ReadableStream.lock() and call controller.error/close as appropriate. Provide helper `withAbort(iter, signal)` to avoid leaks.

Backpressure: on Node and Deno, use stream locks and await writer.ready where available. Expose opt-in `backpressureHint` param (low|medium|high) that maps to chunk size and checkpoint cadence. Provide runtime-specific implementations: Node native streams via stream.Readable.from() fallback for older Node versions.

Retries: SDK will serialize `checkpoint` verbatim into the follow-up request. Server teams will need to implement resume endpoints; for now, implement conservative client-side guardrails: time-limited checkpoints (TTL), and transparent fallthrough to full restart if server rejects checkpoint.
test_plan: Unit tests: core conversion utilities, checkpoint emission frequency, HMAC nonces, and checkpoint format validation.
Integration tests: Node/Browser/Deno runtime matrix verifying cancellation propagation, backpressure behavior, and resume handshake (server stub that accepts checkpoint tokens and returns suffix).
Stress tests: long-running streams (hours) with frequent consumer restarts to validate checkpoint growth, memory usage, and no leaks.
Fuzz tests: malformed checkpoints and server rejections to ensure SDK falls back to full restart without data corruption.
E2E example app: chat replay where a client intentionally loses connection at checkpoint N and resumes to display stream suffix to user.
rollout_plan: Feature flagged behind `ts.progressive_hydrate` for first 2 weeks; enable for internal customers and early-access beta testers.
Step 1: land core utilities and unit tests (feature flag off).
Step 2: enable flag for internal dogfooding and run integration matrix on CI with small server stub.
Step 3: open beta: enable flag for 10% of public requests via client opt-in; collect telemetry (checkpoint acceptance rate, resume success, average checkpoint spacing).
Step 4: iterate on defaults (checkpoint cadence) based on observed latency/cost tradeoffs; then GA and document migration guide.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: checkpoint tokens increase surface area for security issues. Mitigation: make tokens opaque HMACs and set short TTL by default; document correct usage and ensure server rejects stale tokens gracefully.

Risk: different runtimes have divergent backpressure semantics leading to bursts. Mitigation: runtime-specific implementations + conservative defaults; provide opt-in stronger backpressure mode for latency-sensitive apps.

Risk: users may depend on checkpoint consistency across model upgrades. Mitigation: warn in docs that checkpoints are only stable for compatible server-model+version combos and should be used as advisory resume points, not as authoritative transaction logs.
Risk: added complexity in SDK surface. Mitigation: keep public API minimal and provide high-level helpers (`resumeOrRestart`) to cover common patterns.

Risk: server storage for mapping tokens to cursors could be costly if naive. Mitigation: server teams should implement compact cursor snapshots and TTL cleanup; we will add per-checkpoint size limits in the spec.
comments: 2026-03-02 Sana Patel: Initial spike complete. Prototype emits base64 checkpoint every 512 tokens and works across Node 20/22 and Chrome 118. See link to prototype gist: https://gist.github.com/sana/prog-hydrate-spike (internal).

2026-03-04 Liam O'Connor: Reviewed prototype. Main ask: make checkpoint emission pluggable by delimiter and by predicate (user-provided function). Also ensure iterator.return() cleans up locks in all runtimes.

2026-03-07 Devon Ruiz: Suggest using HKDF-derived short token instead of raw HMAC to allow future key rotation semantics. Also add telemetry event names: checkpoint_emitted, checkpoint_resume_attempt, checkpoint_resume_success, checkpoint_fallback_restart.
2026-03-09 QA (Maya Chen): Added test failures around stream.close ordering in Safari; flagged for follow-up to add small Safari-specific shim in runtime detect layer.
